record.question:
A company serves static content through the default domain name of an Amazon CloudFront distribution, such as d123example.cloudfront.net. It does not use an alternate domain name. Every applicable cache behavior must deliver content to viewers only over HTTPS.

Which settings provide the required viewer connection? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Set the Viewer Protocol Policy on each applicable cache behavior to HTTPS Only or Redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Install a self-signed certificate on the S3 origin and leave the Viewer Protocol Policy set to allow HTTP and HTTPS.
Use the default CloudFront certificate for the distribution’s cloudfront.net domain name.
Install a self-signed certificate on an origin load balancer and rely on it to authenticate the viewer-to-CloudFront connection.
Use the origin load balancer’s default DNS name as the viewer certificate for the CloudFront distribution.

explanation.text:
<<1>> controls whether a viewer request can receive content over HTTP. HTTPS Only rejects HTTP requests, while Redirect HTTP to HTTPS directs supported requests to the secure URL. <<3>> supplies the AWS-managed certificate appropriate for the default cloudfront.net hostname. Together they cover protocol enforcement and server authentication.

<<2>> leaves viewers able to use HTTP and proposes an origin setting instead of a viewer control. <<4>> also confuses the origin TLS connection with the viewer connection. <<5>> treats a DNS name as a certificate and uses the wrong hostname for the viewer endpoint.

Viewer and origin transport are separate connections. Requiring viewer HTTPS does not itself establish HTTPS from CloudFront to a custom origin. An alternate viewer domain would also require a certificate covering that domain instead of the default CloudFront certificate.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/using-https-viewers-to-cloudfront.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/latest/APIReference/API_ViewerCertificate.html

diagram_alt: Protocol enforcement and the default viewer certificate apply to the viewer connection; the origin is a separate connection.

sources.supports: Viewer protocol policy, HTTPS rejection/redirect behavior and default CloudFront domain certificate.
CloudFrontDefaultCertificate is used when the distribution has no aliases.

editorial_notes: Removed duplicated correct choices by separating protocol enforcement from certificate selection.
